job.theme: the life of a famous Indian scientist
job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and Dr. Homi Bhabha were two pillars of Indian science who shaped the nation's future. While Bhabha focused on nuclear energy to provide electricity, Sarabhai looked toward the stars to improve communication. In 1962, Sarabhai established the Indian National Committee for Space Research. He believed that space technology was essential because it could bridge the gap between rural villages and modern information. Unlike Bhabha, who worked primarily in the laboratories of Mumbai, Sarabhai spent much of his time in Ahmedabad. By 1969, this committee evolved into the Indian Space Research Organisation, known as ISRO. Sarabhai often argued that the growth of a nation depends on its ability to use technology for the common man. He was not interested in power for its own sake, but in the practical application of science. While Bhabha’s work on atomic reactors required massive infrastructure, Sarabhai’s satellite projects required vast networks of ground stations. Both men faced immense challenges, yet their different approaches ensured that India became a leader in both nuclear and space sectors. Their legacies remain distinct; Bhabha is remembered as the father of the nuclear program, while Sarabhai is celebrated as the visionary behind India's space journey.
response.summary: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and Dr. Homi Bhabha were influential Indian scientists who developed different fields. Bhabha focused on nuclear energy, while Sarabhai pioneered space technology to help the common man.
